title: DaisyChain opportunity field notes
content:
Quick summary:
- Prospect: DaisyChain Logistics (regional 3PL focused on last-mile delivery for DTC brands). Seeded in Midwest, expanding west coast. ~125 employees, recently raised Series A (public note in TechPulse).
- Why they matter: heavy batch NLP needs for routing/agent assist, high call volume, current provider is monolithic cloud vendor charging per-request; they mentioned latency spikes during holiday peaks. Good surface area for Redwood Dedicated or Private (data isolation + predictable throughput).

Top-line hypothesis:
- Starter pilot: integrate Redwood hosted API for a customer support agent assist (intent classification + response drafts) and measure token cost + latency under peak load. If latency/cost looks good, propose a Dedicated pool for fixed throughput and predictable SLOs.

Notes from quick research (public + sales intel):
- Key contacts: CTO = Carla Voss (linkedin: carlavoss), Head of Ops = Miguel Torres (manages carrier ops, likely pilot owner), Dir. CS = Renee Park (owns support tools).
- Technical stack hints: uses Node.js/Typescript, Kafka for events, Redis for short-term state. Prefers vendor-managed SaaS but will consider VPC for compliance.
- Pain signals: complaints about cost during November spikes, two incidents last Q with 2–3s service latency under load. Target metric: median latency < 200ms for interactive agent flows.

Product fit bullets (angles to test with prospect):
- Cost predictability: propose Dedicated reservation to cap unit economics for seasonal spikes.
- Latency: bundling Redwood’s continuous batching + prefix cache can reduce tail latency vs their existing setup.
- Data controls: Private/VPC option for sensitive customer PII in returns/refunds workflows.
- Observability: Redwood Console per-route traces and token-level cost breakdown for their finance & ops teams.

Possible objections and quick responses (first-pass):
- "We already have a relationship with CloudX and engineers are comfortable there."
  -> Response: Acknowledge relationship; offer a 4–6 week proof-of-concept to compare cost/latency on real traffic — low friction (hosted API), no long-term lock-in; emphasize transparent billing and rollout controls.
- "Switching introduces risk during peak season."
  -> Response: Recommend pilot in a non-peak region/queue, can use canary rollouts + automatic fallback to CloudX model; Redwood supports A/B and gradual traffic shift.
- "We need on-prem or VPC for compliance."
  -> Response: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem options and integrates with KMS/HSM; share enterprise datasheet and compliance checklist.

Cold email / Sequence (iterative drafts) — keep short, test subject lines:
- Subject v1: "Cut last-mile support costs during peak season"
  Email v1: "Hey Miguel — quick note: saw DaisyChain call volume spikes during Nov/Dec. We helped a 3PL reduce per-interaction cost by ~40% and cut median agent assist latency by ~60% using a dedicated inference pool. Can I share a 10‑min benchmark plan next week? — Maya"

- Follow-up v1 (3 days): "Still exploring ways to stabilize costs during peak? I can run a no-commit benchmark on a small subset of traffic (hosted API) and share hard numbers."

- Value-add email (if no reply): include a short screenshot mock of Redwood Console cost breakdown (note: attach later) and a 1‑pager on rollout safety (canary + fallback).

Call script bullet points (10–12 min exploratory):
- 1 min: quick intros + one-line value prop (predictable cost + reliable low-latency inference).
- 2–3 min: get them to confirm pain: "What happens to support response times and costs during Black Friday?"
- 3–4 min: discuss technical fit: Node.js + Kafka hooks, how we'd accept event stream and return suggestions; ask about current model provider and quantization concerns.
- 2 min: propose a minimal pilot: 2–4 weeks, 1000–5000 interactions/day, hosted API to compare baseline metrics, success metric = cost per completed interaction and median latency.
- 1 min: next steps and owners.

Risks / unknowns to validate during discovery:
- Data retention policy on their side and requirement for HSM/KMS.
- Exact peak qps and typical sequence lengths (median tokens).
- Whether support UI can accept streaming tokens (for real-time agent assist).

Hypothesis tests for a pilot (measurable):
- Setup: mirror 10% of support traffic for 2 weeks through Redwood hosted API.
- Metrics to capture: per-token spend, median and 95th latency, fallback rate to CloudX, agent satisfaction (survey).
- Success criteria: >=20% cost reduction or median latency < baseline by 30% with equal or higher agent satisfaction.

Proposal sketch for next phase (if pilot passes):
- Option A: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) sized to their peak QPS + autoscale buffer for holiday bursts; monthly commit with overage rules.
- Option B: Private VPC for full data isolation + professional services for on-prem integration.

Open questions / TODO (my checklist):
- [ ] Find exact support QPS numbers (ask Miguel).
- [ ] Get sample traces or anonymized prompts (for eval).
- [ ] Confirm legal/compliance contacts for NDA + data flow.
- [ ] Draft short benchmark plan (template) and send as attachment in 1st follow-up.
- [ ] Create a rough cost model comparing CloudX vs Redwood Dedicated for their likely 4-week peak.

Local notes to self (voice-of-sales shorthand):
- Lean on cost predictability — finance will care most. Ops wants latency guarantees. Engineering worried about integration effort.
- Bring an SRE/solutions engineer early if they ask about rolling window KV cache behavior — likely to be a question.
- Use past case study "ParcelPilot" numbers when sharing reduction stats but flag as non-identifying.

Raw outbound variations to A/B test in sequence (short forms):
- Variation A (ops angle): "Stabilize delivery support during spikes — quick benchmark?"
- Variation B (fin ops angle): "How much could you save on per-interaction AI costs?"
- Variation C (technical): "Can we run a 2-week latency + cost comparison on actual traffic?"

Final: next action planned — schedule intro with Miguel and bring Priya (solutions engineer) to discovery call. Aim to have benchmark plan sent within 72 hours of first reply.

Notes-to-self: keep document updated after call. Capture any quoted numbers from prospect in a follow-up email to create shared record.
